rationale: ROUND 3 on 0b84970d — POST-APPROVAL HARDENING, submitted so the trail reflects what actually shipped rather than because a verdict demands it: round 2 was APPROVED (2026-08-25 21:21), and the next day an independent adversarial review (fresh-context reviewer, different model, read-only licence, run at the user's request over the committed code, the live DB and these submissions) found three real defects in the approved layer that neither council round nor I had. All are fixed in commit d547b54cc and this round shows them. (1) THE STAMP DISCRIMINATOR COULD DOUBLE-DELIVER. AlreadyHandedOver was `handed_over_at <> $2` — which conflates 'I stamped just now' with 'someone stamped with my exact timestamp'. pgx v5 encodes timestamptz at microsecond precision, so two Claims colliding in one microsecond BOTH read not-already; worse and needing no collision at all, ANY caller that retries with the same `now` (a timestamp hoisted out of a retry loop, or derived from a work item) gets not-already on every retry, deterministically — each retry minting a fresh token and sending a fresh delivery email. My round-2 grounded_in told this council StampHandover has 'no read-then-write, no window': true of the row update, false of the discriminator, and I state that correction here plainly. The claim is now the WHERE clause — `AND handed_over_at IS NULL` matches for at most one winner by construction; the loser lands in ErrNoRows and reads the winner's stamp; no timestamp takes part in the decision. PROVEN on real Postgres in a rolled-back transaction with the disconfirming control: second same-timestamp claim returned UPDATE 0, while the OLD discriminator evaluated on the same state answered 'NOT already — would DOUBLE-DELIVER'. (2) THE FILING CONTRACT WAS HALF-STATED. HandleApproveWorkItem has a SECOND 400 after the status check — `spec.checkpoint` must be true — and its error text ('use retry or resolve instead') steers the owner to RESOLVE, which writes `resolved_by`, the key the gate deliberately ignores. A producer honouring only ReviewItemFiledStatus files a review nobody can approve; delivery stalls forever while every button press appears to succeed — the same silent-stall class round 2 was approved for closing, one guard further along. ReviewItemRequiredSpec() now pins the spec half of the contract (fresh map per call, shared-map mutation asserted against). (3) MY OWN CENSUS REPEATED THE ARCHIVE MISTAKE. The approved round's grounded_in claimed 'the approve path has never been exercised in production' — measured on the LIVE table only, the exact omission Reviewed() exists to correct. The archive holds ONE approved_by row (needs_brief_review, completed 2026-03-17, created_by='test'). Corrected visibly in the doc comment; it also usefully proves approved_by survives archival in the wild. TWO FURTHER REVIEW FINDINGS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT PATCHED and are recorded in DGH-017 as residuals: UpdateWorkItemStatusAction's non-complete branch has no status guard and merges result forward (a reopened review's approval survives; and the gate has no revocation — bounded by Claim being once-only), and HandleUpdateWorkItem lets an admin PATCH re-type any approved checkpoint item into a delivery approval. Both live in shared admin/work-item machinery; patching them inside this lane's round would be the bugs_closed/124 bundling. Named here so the seats can overrule that scoping if they judge otherwise.

plan.summary: Post-approval hardening of the approved claim layer (commit d547b54cc): StampHandover's at-most-once discriminator becomes the WHERE clause (`AND handed_over_at IS NULL`; ErrNoRows arm reads the winner's stamp) instead of a timestamp comparison that double-delivered on equal or reused `now` values; ReviewItemRequiredSpec() pins the spec half of the filing contract (checkpoint:true) that the approve handler enforces with a 400 whose advice steers toward the wrong button; the 'never exercised' doc claim is corrected (the archive holds one approved_by row); and handover.go's two stale single-use comments describing the retired pre-second-click design are fixed. Tests updated to pin the claim predicate by regex; three mutations killed; SQL semantics proven on real Postgres rolled-back with the old discriminator as the control.

edits.symbol: StampHandover — the claim moves into the WHERE clause; plus two stale single-use comments in the same file corrected
edits.rationale: The at-most-once property must not depend on `now` being unique per call, and it did: `RETURNING ... handed_over_at <> $2` reads false for a same-microsecond collision AND for any retry that reuses its timestamp, making both callers proceed to mint and email. Now `WHERE id=$1 AND handed_over_at IS NULL` admits at most one winner by construction: a concurrent second caller blocks on the row lock, re-evaluates the WHERE after commit (READ COMMITTED), matches nothing, and the ErrNoRows arm reads the committed stamp via Get — which also distinguishes 'already stamped' from 'no such site'. live_link_expires_at keeps its COALESCE so an independently-set expiry is never overwritten. SAME FILE, SAME COMMIT: ConfirmTransfer's comment claimed 'the token itself is single-use, so the second click fails at RedeemToken' — the retired pre-second-click design, FALSE of the running code (prepare.go mints confirm tokens singleUse=false, deliberately) — and MintToken's parameter doc named the confirm link as its worked example of single-use. Both corrected visibly with the reasoning that survives: the COALESCE is the only belt and it is sufficient, since nothing is protected by spending the token.

The status was not the whole filing contract: after the needs_human_review check, HandleApproveWorkItem refuses any item whose spec lacks checkpoint:true (site_admin_handlers.go:1074-1078), with advice pointing at the resolve button — whose resolved_by the gate ignores. The producer contract now has both halves as code. And the doc's 'never exercised in production' line is corrected in place, marked as a correction with the date and what caught it, per the working-docs rules: the census behind it read the live table only.

edits.symbol: expectStamp pins the claim predicate; the checkpoint-contract test
edits.rationale: expectStamp now matches the claim by regex — `(?s)UPDATE sites.*handed_over_at IS NULL` — so reverting to the timestamp discriminator fails three tests rather than passing silently; 'already handed over' is modelled as it now happens (claim returns no rows, then the stamp read). TestReviewItemRequiredSpecCarriesTheCheckpointFlag pins the spec contract and asserts the map is fresh per call.

grounded_in: THE RACE, PROVEN ON REAL POSTGRES 2026-08-26 in a rolled-back transaction (the package's own stated convention for SQL semantics sqlmock cannot hold): claim 1 with timestamp T returned 'CLAIM1 won' / UPDATE 1; claim 2 with the SAME T returned zero rows / UPDATE 0; and the CONTROL — the old discriminator `handed_over_at <> T` evaluated on the resulting state — answered 'NOT already -> would DOUBLE-DELIVER'. The measurement could have come out the other way and for the old code it did.

THE DRIVER FACT the collision arm rests on: platform/database/postgres.go uses jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib, which encodes timestamptz at microsecond precision — so 'same timestamp' is a one-microsecond window, not a nanosecond one, and the reused-`now` retry shape needs no collision at all.

THE CHECKPOINT GUARD, read at the handler: site_admin_handlers.go:1074-1078 — `isCheckpoint, _ := spec["checkpoint"].(bool); if !isCheckpoint { 400 "this item is not a checkpoint — use retry or resolve instead" }`, AFTER the needs_human_review check my round-2 submission pinned; plus `ReviewData json.RawMessage binding:"required"` on the POST body (the admin screen's concern, noted in the doc rather than encoded).

THE ARCHIVE ROW REFUTING MY ROUND-2 CLAIM, measured 2026-08-26: `SELECT item_type, status, created_by, completed_at::date, result->>'approved_by' FROM site_work_items_archive WHERE result ? 'approved_by'` returns exactly one row — needs_brief_review | complete | test | 2026-03-17 | admin. My round-2 grounded_in said 'ZERO carry approved_by ... never been exercised' from a live-table-only census. The correction is in the code comment, in WRONG_CALLS.md, and here.

MUTATIONS RUN 2026-08-26, each restored, clean suite green at -count=1: reverting StampHandover's WHERE to the timestamp discriminator FAILS three tests via expectStamp's pinned regex; ReviewItemRequiredSpec returning checkpoint:false (or a shared map) FAILS its test. verify-head-builds.sh --test green against HEAD 1e37f282a with all changed files overlaid.

THE TWO UNPATCHED RESIDUALS, with their evidence so the scoping can be judged: (a) UpdateWorkItemStatusAction's non-complete branch (v3_site_actions.go:6321-6327) — `UPDATE site_work_items SET status=$2, ... result = COALESCE(result,'{}') || $3` with NO status precondition, while the complete branch above it carries one; a reopened review keeps approved_by through the merge, and the gate has no revocation since archived rows are effectively immutable. Bounded: Claim is once-only, so exposure is the window before the first Claim. (b) HandleUpdateWorkItem (site_admin_handlers.go:840-921) accepts arbitrary item_type on any row — one PATCH re-types any historically-approved checkpoint item into a needs_delivery_review approval. Admin-only. Both are shared machinery; fixing them here would bundle a shared-seam change into a lane round (bugs_closed/124's veto class). Recorded in DGH-017.

WHAT THE REVIEW DID NOT FIND, so the negatives carry weight: whole-repo, exactly ONE writer of result.approved_by (the approve handler); the on_approve follow-on writes approved_by into SPEC, not result, and lands at triaged — no transitive gate-opener; actions.writeWorkItem cannot write result at all (struct and INSERT column list omit it); the archiver copies status and result verbatim by explicit column list and swaps INSERT+DELETE in one transaction, so the UNION's single snapshot has no gap; no soft-delete column exists to filter; NULL result cannot false-match `? 'approved_by'`.
